reviews.one_line_contribution: A component-wise decomposition of a cross-backbone agent-memory item -- writer's reasoning text vs action-observation sequence vs scaffold -- claiming the reasoning text is the part that fails to travel, with an authorship swap at fixed actions to localise the harm to who wrote the thoughts, and the practical negative result that deterministically deleting the thought slot matches a model-aware LLM rewriter at matched tokens.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified papers threaten different halves. (1) arXiv:2603.13260, 'Explain in Your Own Words: Improving Reasoning via Token-Selective Dual Knowledge Distillation' (verified via s2cli paper, S2, 2026-02-25, 13 citations) is the mechanism itself: the teacher's rationale distribution mismatches the student, and letting the student re-author the rationale in its own words fixes it. The proposal's F3/F5 authorship swap is that step ported in-context, and the proposal concedes as much ('the parametric cousin of the F3 arm'). Novelty therefore rests on substrate (in-context agent memory rather than fine-tuning) and on the thought/action/scaffold decomposition, not on the mechanism. That is a real but incremental delta. (2) arXiv:2212.10001, 'Towards Understanding Chain-of-Thought Prompting: An Empirical Study of What Matters' (verified via the literature command, HF channel) plus arXiv:2401.04925, 'The Impact of Reasoning Step Length on Large Language Models' (same channel), threaten the effect rather than the framing: the demonstration-rationale literature already reports that the content and validity of reasoning in demonstrations matters little while length and relevance matter a lot. That is the prior that makes Delta_strip = 0 the default expectation and makes an unpadded F1r-vs-F2 contrast read as a length result. (3) arXiv:2605.30723 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All' (verified via s2cli paper, S2, 2026-05-29, 2 citations) is the named target and does not scoop: it establishes model-dependent skill utility and trains a rewriter, but never decomposes an item or runs a zero-cost strip. Also adjacent and unnamed by the proposal: arXiv:2608.05784 'Activity Frames' (HF channel) already reports a deterministic compiler beating LLM summaries for agent memory in the screen-capture domain, which softens the surprise of P3's shape. No paper I found makes the central claim.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline writer x reader interaction is confounded with headroom, and the confound is built in by the proposal's own Gate 0. Gate 0 requires S(F1, R->R) - S(F1, W->R) >= 6 net pooled, i.e. the same-backbone cells must sit at least 6 points ABOVE the cross cells before P1 is even framed. P1 then predicts a large strip gain (>= +5) exactly in the low-scoring cross cells and a null (<= +1) exactly in the high-scoring same-backbone cells. A reader with no provenance mechanism at all -- just compression toward a ceiling, or diminishing returns of any context manipulation as base success rises toward the 0.81/0.87 range Measurement A already observed for Q with k=3 -- reproduces P1(a), P1(b) and the >= +4 interaction. The proposal's stated defence, that the same-backbone cells 'inject the very strings the cross cells inject', answers the token-bloat alternative but not this one: identical strings do not equalise the room a cell has to move. No arm varies headroom at fixed provenance (no difficulty-stratified reanalysis, no handicapped same-backbone cell, no cross cell matched on base success), so the headline estimand cannot separate 'foreign thoughts are noise' from 'strip helps wherever there is room'. Two lesser versions of the same problem: F4's hard truncation to F2's token count can mangle rewriter output and biases Delta_rewrite toward the predicted null, so P3's marquee 'a parser matches a model' claim is partly manufactured by the cap and by using a prompted rather than trained rewriter; and F5's foreign thoughts are teacher-forced over actions the foreign backbone would not have chosen, so provenance is confounded with rationalising a disagreed-with sequence, which F5-self (same author, actions it did choose) cannot calibrate.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Promote the within-cell authorship arms to the headline. F5 (reader Q's own actions, thoughts by Q vs by E vs by G, length-matched) and F4a/F3 are single-cell, single-reader, fixed-base-rate contrasts with no headroom confound; P5 is the strongest prediction in the design and should carry the title, with the F1r/F2 cross-vs-same interaction demoted to corroboration. (2) Add a headroom control to P1: pre-register a difficulty-stratified reanalysis of Delta_strip against per-game base success, and add one same-backbone cell handicapped to the cross cells' F1r success level (e.g. by subsampling or degrading the retrieved pool) so a matched-base-rate same-backbone Delta_strip exists; if the strip gain tracks base success rather than writer identity, the mismatch claim fails. (3) Add the length-matched filler arm inside the cross cells (below). (4) Fix the F5 disagreement confound: log, per forced step, whether the thought-author would have chosen that action under its own policy, stratify P5 by agreement rate, and add an arm where Q rationalises a Q-authored action sequence from a different item (own author, own policy, disagreed-with sequence) to separate authorship from disagreement. (5) Run F4 uncapped at its natural token length as well as capped, and report the strip-vs-rewriter comparison at both matched and natural tokens with cost alongside; a 'matched at matched tokens' claim against a baseline that truncation may have broken will not survive review. (6) Adopt the entailment check's P6 fix (one same-backbone F6 cell and one minimum-deficit cross F6 cell, pre-registered before Phase A is unblinded), since the current two F6 cells are selected on an outcome-correlated criterion.
reviews.missing_baseline: A length-matched thought placebo inside the cross cells: F2 padded back to F1r's exact token count with content-free or provenance-neutral text, and/or with the same writer's thoughts taken from a different (mismatched) retrieved item at matched length and style. The plan controls for length only ACROSS cells (the same-backbone cells are called 'the control for length per se'), never WITHIN a cross cell, so Delta_strip = S(F2) - S(F1r) remains a joint content-plus-length contrast in exactly the cells the headline is computed on. This is not a nicety: arXiv:2401.04925 reports that reasoning-step length alone moves demonstration effects even when the rationale content is wrong, and arXiv:2212.10001 reports that rationale validity contributes little relative to surface properties. A filler arm also splits the claim in a way the title needs -- 'the writer's reasoning CONTENT is non-transferable' versus 'any ~N tokens of prose wedged between the action lines dilute a foreign item' -- and it is cheap (one extra serialization on the existing 6 cross cells, no new pool, no new model pass).

ID verification: I verified every arXiv ID the proposal's novelty argument leans on. Via s2cli paper: 2605.30723 (S2, 2026-05-29, 2 cit), 2608.06880 (2026-08-07), 2606.01311 (S2, 9 cit), 2606.01139 (S2, 12 cit), 2605.11032 (Portable Agent Memory, S2, 3 cit), 2603.13260 (S2, 2026-02-25, 13 cit), 2509.23574 (EMNLP, 7 cit). Assessment of the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: above average and honest -- it names its channel, gives three query classes with returned IDs, states plainly that no new citation was added, and correctly identifies 2603.13260 as its parametric cousin rather than hiding it. Its one real blind spot is that all four queries live in the agent/skill/distillation vocabulary; it never searches the in-context demonstration-design literature, which is where the results that most threaten the predicted effect size sit (2212.10001, 2401.04925, 2311.09277). Those papers do not scoop the claim, but a check that had found them would have been forced to add the length-matched filler arm before submission.

reviews.one_line_contribution: When a stored agent trajectory is reused by a different backbone, the transferable part is the action-observation sequence and the lost part is the writer's reasoning text, so a zero-cost deterministic parser that deletes the thought slot recovers the cross-backbone deficit, the harm tracks who authored the thoughts rather than who authored the actions, and a model-aware LLM rewriter buys nothing over the strip at matched tokens.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, neither fatal. (1) arXiv:2605.30723, 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment for LLM Agents' (verified via the literature command, S2, 2026-05-29, 2 citations) already establishes the premise the proposal builds on -- skill utility is model-dependent and reusing one formulation across backbones is wrong -- and supplies the rewriter the proposal wants to beat. It does not decompose an item into thought/action/scaffold and does not run an action-only strip as a baseline, so the strip-vs-rewriter comparison is genuinely open; but this means the proposal's contribution is an ablation and a missing baseline for an existing paper, which is a real but modest increment. (2) The sharper threat to the mechanism is arXiv:2509.23196, 'From Harm to Help: Turning Reasoning In-Context Demos into Assets for Reasoning LMs' (verified, S2, 2025-09-27), which already reports that reasoning traces inside in-context demonstrations HARM reasoning LMs and fixes it by converting demos into insights (I2S/I2S+) across open- and closed-source models. 'Foreign reasoning text in a demonstration is the harmful component' is therefore not new as a phenomenon; what is new here is localizing it to a writer x reader interaction with the author of the thoughts swapped at fixed actions (F3/F5) inside an agent-memory store. Note also that I2S+ is an existence proof that an LLM conversion step CAN beat the raw demos, which is exactly P3's falsifier -- the proposal should cite it and explain why its rewriter is expected to fail where I2S succeeded. Parametric cousins, all verified: arXiv:2603.13260 'Explain in Your Own Words' (token-selective dual KD, 13 cit), arXiv:2509.22230 'In Their Own Words: Reasoning Traces Tailored for Small Models', arXiv:2512.20908 (provenance tracing in reasoning distillation, 7 cit), arXiv:2306.14050 (SCoTD, 241 cit); the proposal correctly identifies these as the training-time analog of F3 and they do not pre-empt the in-context form. Adjacent and uncited: arXiv:2604.01029 'Revision or Re-Solving? Decomposing Second-Pass Gains in Multi-LLM Pipelines' (verified, 2 cit) decomposes multi-LLM second-pass gains into re-solving, scaffold and content components -- the same decompose-the-gain-into-components move in a neighbouring setting.
reviews.strongest_objection: The plan cannot decide its own headline at the power it has, and it says so. Every pass/fail criterion separates a predicted value from a falsifier by 2 to 3 net points (P1: +5 vs +3; P2: +2 vs +4; P3: +2 vs +4; P4b: 2 vs 5) against pooled half-widths of +/-1.2 to +/-2.6. Those half-widths are manufactured by two scalings of Measurement C's single measured number (+/-5.25 paired at 274 games x 2 seeds), and both scalings assume variance this design does not have. First, sqrt(2/S) over seeds: seeds re-run the SAME fixed 274 validation games, so extra seeds shrink only the decoding-stochasticity component, while the between-game component -- which is precisely what the pre-registered game-cluster bootstrap keeps inside the interval -- does not shrink at all. Six seeds therefore cannot deliver +/-3.0 per cell if the paired contrast at two seeds is +/-5.25 and most of that width is between-game. Second, 1/sqrt(cells): the six cross cells share the same 274 games and, within a writer, the same retrieved items and the same injected strings, so they are strongly positively correlated and pooling does not buy sqrt(6). The proposal concedes the second point and pre-registers a fallback -- 'if the realized pooled width exceeds 1.5x the design figure, per-cell criteria are reported as the result' -- but per-cell widths are +/-3.0 to +/-4.3, which cannot distinguish Delta_strip = +5 from the +3 falsifier in any cell. The pre-registered fallback is thus a design in which P1, P2, P3 and P4(b) are all undecidable, and nothing in the plan can add power: ALFWorld's validation split caps N at 274 games, and the episode budget is already 60,300. The likely paper is six directional point estimates with overlapping intervals and a title that asserts a decomposition the intervals do not support. A secondary form of the same objection: Gate 0, which establishes that there IS a cross-backbone deficit to decompose, is explicitly 'framing only' and P1-P6 run regardless -- so the paper is guaranteed to be written even if the phenomenon its title names does not exist, and the pre-registered fallback framing ('harm-and-removal rather than deficit recovery') quietly abandons 'the non-transferable part of cross-backbone agent experience' while keeping the headline.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-derive the noise model empirically instead of by scaling. Measurement C's runs are on disk: bootstrap the realized paired k3-static3 contrast at one seed versus two to measure the actual seed-reducible fraction of the +/-5.25, and jointly bootstrap two cells that share games to measure the cell-cell correlation. Set seeds and cells from those two numbers, and pre-register margins that survive them. (2) If +/-1.2 is unreachable -- it probably is -- restate P1 as a within-pool paired interaction rather than a pooled difference of pooled means: for each writer pool W, compute Delta_strip(W->R) - Delta_strip(W->W) on the same items and the same games, which is a paired quantity with the pool-quality confound differenced out (as pooled, the interaction compares cells built from different pools, so 'E's thoughts are simply worse/longer than Q's, and stripping bad thoughts helps everyone' is not excluded by the current estimand). Then a sign test over the six within-pool interactions is a criterion the design can actually meet. (3) Add the token-matched irrelevant-thought placebo described below. (4) Take the entailment check's P6 fix verbatim: pre-register one same-backbone F6 cell and one cross F6 cell at the SMALLEST Phase-A verbatim deficit, so 'thoughts carry the procedure' has a cell where it could appear; selecting both F6 cells on largest deficit selects on an outcome-correlated criterion. (5) Drop P4(b) as a prediction or give it an arm -- as written DoD = (P4a - P1a) + P1b up to the F5-self offset and adds no evidence. (6) Use the on-disk expert pool as the highest-powered positive control for the authorship claim: X is already stripped and its gain for Q is measured (+17.2 over static3, CI +/-5), so X actions plus foreign teacher-forced thoughts versus X in F2 form tests 'adding foreign thoughts destroys transfer' in the one cell where the baseline is known rather than assumed. That arm is cheap, uses data already collected, and would carry the paper even if the Q/E/G matrix comes back noisy. (7) Fix the abstract's 'byte-identical injected strings': the retrieved items are shared, the serialized context is not, since F1r/F2 re-render into each reader's scaffold template.
reviews.missing_baseline: A token-matched irrelevant-thought placebo: the writer's own thoughts taken from a DIFFERENT episode (or a different task type), spliced onto the retrieved actions at matched per-step length. Without it, 'the harm follows the author of the thoughts' (P4, P5) is not separated from 'the harm follows any thought text that was not generated for these actions'. F5-E and F5-G are teacher-forced rationalizations of action sequences their authors would not have chosen, so foreign authorship and post-hoc incoherence vary together, and the single F5-self offset arm calibrates post-hoc-ness only in the matched-author case; F6 (thoughts only) is a content placebo, not a length-matched noise placebo, and blind1 is a wrong-type ITEM placebo measured under k=0 in a different experiment and explicitly not re-run. The brief's own binding rule ('token- and rate-matched placebos', 'contamination arms are manufactured, gated and positively controlled') asks for exactly this arm. Second omission a reviewer will name: an F2-at-matched-tokens arm. F2 deletes tokens and holds k=3, so the practical recommendation ('strip the thoughts') frees budget that a competitor would spend on more items; F2 at k=5-7 to match F1r's token count would show whether the strip's advantage survives when the reader could instead have had more demonstrations, and it is the arm that decides whether the result is a claim about thoughts or a claim about context budget.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round -- it names the channel (s2cli.py, S2 + HF, both 'ok'), states that WebSearch was unavailable, reports three query classes (recent mechanism, home literature, closest named method) and returns IDs rather than assertions -- and I verified the IDs it leans on: 2605.30723 (S2, 2026-05-29, 2 cit, exactly the Model-Aware Skill Alignment paper described), 2608.06880 SkillAligner, 2606.01311 SkillAdaptor (9 cit), 2606.01139 SkillRevise, 2603.13260 'Explain in Your Own Words' (13 cit), 2512.20908 (7 cit), 2509.23574 MoRSD, 2306.14050 SCoTD (241 cit), 2608.24232 TRACE and 2608.10232 FACT -- the last two are a reasoning-safety benchmark and a world-action model respectively, i.e. false positives the proposal listed without noting that they are off-topic. 2605.11032 failed a direct id lookup and I recovered it only through a search: 'Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Cryptographically-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous AI Agents' (S2, 2026-05-10, 3 cit) -- verified, though it is a protocol/SDK artifact, so the Related Work claim that its rehydration step is a serious uncompared adaptation baseline is weaker than stated. My own queries, all answered by the literature command (channel (a); WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch never used): (i) recent, 'removing reasoning traces from in-context demonstrations improves cross-model transfer action-only' -> 2509.23196, 2509.22230, 2606.00642, 2604.01161, 2512.20908, 2510.11545, 2509.13237 -- the first two are the notable misses; (ii) all-years, 'chain-of-thought demonstrations from a different model hurt in-context learning reasoning style mismatch' -> 2409.04057, 2311.09277, 2401.04925, 2410.21333, 2402.16048, nothing closer than the novelty card already showed; (iii) recent, closest named method, 'model-aware rewriter adapts retrieved skill to target backbone versus no adaptation baseline' -> 2605.30723, 2608.06880, 2606.01139, 2605.09359, 2608.03874, 2604.01029 -- confirming no strip baseline in that family and surfacing 2604.01029 as an uncited decomposition analog; (iv) recent, 'agent experience memory stores trajectories action observation only without reasoning thoughts reused by another backbone' -> 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2607.10608 'The Compliance Trap', 2608.04530 FocusMem, 2605.24468 SAM -- none decomposes a stored item into thought versus action; (v) recent, 'portable memory format protocol transfer agent memory across models rehydration' -> 2605.11032 (verification), 2608.07169, 2608.11224, 2606.05684. The material gap in the proposal's check is that its recent-mechanism query used agent/experience vocabulary and therefore missed the in-context CoT-demo-harm line: 2509.23196 reports that reasoning demonstrations harm reasoning LMs and that an LLM conversion step turns them into an asset, and 2509.22230 reports that teacher traces are distributionally misaligned for small students and must be re-authored 'in their own words'. Neither manipulates writer identity at fixed actions, neither is agentic, and neither runs a deterministic action-only strip, so the central claim is not scooped -- but the claim's premise (foreign reasoning text in context is the harmful component) is already published, and the check's conclusion 'no collision found; no new citation was added in this revision' overstates what the searches licensed. Novelty is scored on that basis: the phenomenon is known, the decomposition and the authorship swap are the new part.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A component-decomposition of cross-backbone agent experience: at fixed retrieved items, fixed reader scaffold and matched tokens, deleting the writer's ReAct/think text (not converting the scaffold, and not paying for a model-aware rewriter) is claimed to recover most of the cross-backbone deficit, with authorship-swap arms (reader's own post-hoc thoughts over foreign actions, foreign thoughts over the reader's own actions) locating the harm in who wrote the reasoning rather than in the item as a whole.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, neither fatal. (1) arXiv:2605.30723 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment' (verified via s2cli, S2, 2026-05-29, 2 citations) is the named target: it establishes that skill utility is model-dependent and trains a lightweight rewriter to fix it. It does not decompose an item into thought vs action vs scaffold and does not run a delete-the-reasoning baseline, so it threatens P3's framing more than P1's claim — but the proposal only reimplements it as a *prompted* rewriter, so it does not actually contest 2605.30723's result. (2) arXiv:2509.23196 'From Harm to Help: Turning Reasoning In-Context Demos into Assets for Reasoning LMs' (verified, S2, 2025-09-27), which I found and the proposal did not cite, already documents the phenomenon-level claim that in-context demos carrying another model's reasoning *harm* reasoning LMs and proposes a test-time rewrite (Insight-to-Solve) as the fix. It is on QA/math, not agent experience memory; it does not manipulate writer identity, does not hold retrieved items fixed across serializations, and its baseline is direct answering rather than a stripped demo — so the proposal's cross-backbone estimand and its zero-cost-strip-vs-rewriter contest survive, but 'foreign reasoning text in the context hurts' is no longer a surprising claim, and a reviewer will read the title as overselling a known effect. Also relevant and uncited: arXiv:2403.14589 (ActRe/A3T, verified, S2, 19 citations) already generates post-hoc reasons for arbitrary action sequences, which is the F3/F5 teacher-forcing device applied to training data rather than in-context; and arXiv:2605.23899 (verified, S2, 15 citations) already reports that neither extractors nor consumers behave uniformly and that model-generated skills show non-trivial negative transfer.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline interaction P1(c) is partly manufactured by headroom, not by producer-consumer mismatch. The same-backbone cells are the only control that excludes a pure token-efficiency/dead-weight account, and the proposal's own Step-0 numbers put a reader with a good pool at 0.807/0.869 success (Measurement A, expert->Q at k=3). A cell sitting at ~0.85 cannot show Delta_strip >= +5 on a percentage-point scale whatever the mechanism, so P1(b) (<= +1 same-backbone) is close to entailed by the ceiling and P1(c) = (a)-(b) inherits that. The design has no headroom correction anywhere: no odds/logit-scale or normalized-gain analysis, no matching of same- and cross-backbone cells on baseline success, no arm that puts a same-backbone cell at cross-cell success level. A reviewer will say the experiment cannot distinguish 'own thoughts are harmless because the reader wrote them' from 'own thoughts have no room to hurt because the cell is near ceiling', which is exactly the alternative P1 was built to exclude. Second, P3's null is nearly engineered: the rewriter is prompted rather than trained (the paper it is aimed at trains one), gets one regeneration and is then hard-truncated to the token count of an action-only strip, with validity checked only as mean tokens within 10% and never for well-formedness. 'A deterministic strip matches a model-aware rewriter' will not be granted from a truncated prompted proxy, and the title asserts it.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Pre-register a scale on which the writer x reader interaction is not ceiling-bound: report Delta_strip on the logit scale and as a fraction of remaining headroom alongside net points, and add one same-backbone cell whose baseline success is matched to the cross cells (e.g. a harder task subset or a degraded same-backbone pool), so P1(b) has room to fail. (2) Add the token-matched filler placebo described below; without it the F1r-F2 contrast is a length contrast with a plausible mechanism attached. (3) Either drop the rewriter claim to 'a prompted model-aware rewriter under a matched token budget adds nothing', or run the rewriter uncapped with tokens reported and score cost-adjusted, so the P3 result is about adaptation rather than about truncation; also report the fraction of F4 items that were truncated mid-item. (4) Fix the F6 selection: as the entailment check notes, choosing the two thoughts-only cells by largest verbatim deficit selects on an outcome-correlated criterion; add one same-backbone F6 cell and one smallest-deficit cross cell, pre-registered before Phase A is unblinded. (5) State the domain limit up front and, if budget allows after the pre-registered cut order, run one cross cell in a second domain (WebShop) — in ALFWorld the action sequence essentially is the procedure, which is the most likely reason the strip wins.
reviews.missing_baseline: A token-matched, content-neutral filler placebo: F1r with the writer's thoughts replaced by an equal number of task-irrelevant or generic text tokens in the same slot (the brief's own Appendix B demands token- and rate-matched placebos, and the wrong-type placebo blind1 is cited from Measurement C rather than re-run here). As written, F1r vs F2 differs in exactly the deleted thought tokens, and the only defense against a pure-length account is the same-backbone cells, which are ceiling-compressed. The filler arm separates 'the foreign author's reasoning specifically hurts' from 'any ~N tokens of non-action prose between the action lines hurt a foreign reader', and it is cheap: two cross cells at 4 seeds. A second, weaker omission: no arm that keeps the writer's thought *content* while normalizing its surface form (deterministic reformatting into the reader's thought template without regeneration), so 'authorship' in P4/P5 is confounded with style plus content plus post-hoc-ness rather than isolated.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision, but the proposal's check is thinner than it presents, and I am scoring novelty on what I verified rather than on its assertions. Every query below ran through the literature command (s2cli.py, Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace Papers, channels s2=ok hf=ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. My queries: (1) mechanism, unrestricted, 'removing chain-of-thought reasoning from in-context demonstrations improves performance action-only exemplars' -> CoT-prompting literature only (2409.04057, 2311.09277, 2410.21333), nothing on cross-model experience items; (2) mechanism, --recent, 'agent experience memory transfer across backbones reasoning traces written by another model hurt reader' -> 2607.28272 MemHarness, 2607.10608 The Compliance Trap, 2606.00642, 2512.16962 MemoryGraft — none decomposes an item into thought vs action; (3) --recent, 'which component of a stored trajectory transfers across models thoughts versus actions ablation memory item' -> memory-architecture papers only, empty on point; (4) closest named method, --recent, 'model-aware skill rewriter baseline deterministic stripping no adaptation matched tokens cross-model skill reuse' -> 2605.30723, 2608.06880, 2606.01139, 2606.01311, plus 2608.11079 and 2608.05604 (two distinct SkillZip papers) — all adapt or compress whole skills, none runs a zero-cost strip as the baseline; (5) 'reasoning style mismatch between demonstration author and consumer model in-context learning negative transfer rationale' -> 2509.23196, 2509.22230, 2504.01738 'Style over Substance', 2601.03717 MIND; (6) --recent, 'in-context demonstrations containing chain-of-thought harm reasoning models remove rationales from demos' -> safety-benchmark noise, empty on point; (7) 'ALFWorld retrieved trajectory exemplars action observation only versus ReAct thought annotated cross model agent success' -> 2403.14589 ActRe, 2505.00234, 2607.13884. Verified IDs the proposal relies on: 2605.30723, 2608.06880, 2606.01311, 2606.01139, 2605.11032, 2603.13260, 2512.20908, 2509.23574, 2306.14050, 2604.15877, 2606.00642, 2604.01161 — all resolve and match their descriptions. Two IDs it lists as evidence do NOT support the claim made for them: 2608.24232 is TRACE, a safety benchmark for reasoning traces, and 2608.10232 is FACT, failure-aware causal training for world-action models in robotics; neither is about in-context demonstrations from another model, so query (1) of the proposal's own check effectively returned nothing on topic and is reported as coverage. 2608.13760 could NOT be verified — not found on S2 or HF. The check also missed the two nearest items I found (2509.23196, 2403.14589) and its home-literature query stopped at parametric distillation, which is where the in-context analog was most likely to have been scooped. Net: novelty is real but narrower than the title, and the collision check earns a deduction rather than a neutral.
